stem: On an O2-saturation plot, which curve has the highest affinity?
options: The curve at lowest pO2 only
rationale: P50 is the pO2 needed for half saturation, so lower P50 means higher affinity.
mediaNote: Use L033 p. 7 saturation-curve graph; learner must identify plotted curve/half-saturation relationship.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: A higher P50 means more pO2 is required for half-saturation and therefore lower, not higher, affinity.

stem: In an H&E dermis field, thick eosinophilic type I collagen bundles run in many directions with sparse ground substance. What tissue is present?
rationale: Dermis is dense irregular CT with multidirectional type I collagen bundles.
mediaNote: Requires the dermis virtual-slide/image series or Figure 3 on Lab L3 p. 6.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: Loose CT has relatively few fibers and more ground substance; thick multidirectional type I bundles identify dense irregular CT.

stem: A tendon shows wavy, parallel collagen bundles and fibroblast nuclei in rows. What property follows?
rationale: Dense regular CT is strong for unidirectional, parallel stress.
mediaNote: Requires the tendon image series on Lab L3 p. 7.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: Parallel tendon collagen resists force along one axis; multidirectional tensile strength is the dense-irregular pattern.

stem: Which fiber/stain pairing is correct in this lab?
options: Type I collagen - dark in silver-stain preparations
Type III reticular - black in silver stain
Type III reticular - thick H&E bundles
rationale: Silver stain delineates type III reticular fibers as black in lymph node.
mediaNote: Requires silver-stain Image Series A on Lab L3 p. 8.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: The lab identifies reticular type III fibers, not type I collagen, as black in the silver-stain lymph-node preparation.

stem: An aortic wall has folded, glassy elastic sheets separated by smooth muscle. What structure is being identified?
rationale: Aortic elastic lamellae are perforated sheets synthesized by smooth muscle.
mediaNote: Requires aortic H&E/toluidine-blue image series on Lab L3 p. 9.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: Elastic fibers occur in ligaments, but the aortic wall contains perforated elastic lamellae between smooth muscle cells.

stem: An H&E cell has a large empty cytoplasmic space and a flattened peripheral nucleus. What is it?
rationale: Lipid is lost in routine preparation, creating the empty-appearing droplet of a unilocular adipocyte.
mediaNote: Requires unilocular-adipocyte virtual slide on Lab L3 p. 9.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: Fibroblasts have elongate nuclei and scant cytoplasm; the empty lipid space with a peripheral nucleus identifies an adipocyte.

stem: Which finding best supports plasma-cell identification?
options: Central nucleus with one lipid droplet
Flattened heterochromatic nucleus between collagen bundles
Eccentric clock-face nucleus and pale Golgi zone
rationale: Plasma cells have eccentric clock-face nuclei, RER-rich basophilic cytoplasm, and a pale Golgi area.
mediaNote: Requires plasma-cell Image Series/EM on Lab L3 p. 12.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: Multilobed nuclei with eosinophilic granules suggest granulocytes, not the eccentric clock-face nucleus and pale Golgi zone of plasma cells.

stem: Which thioglycolate growth pattern identifies a facultative organism?
options: A narrow band below the surface
Growth throughout, greatest at the top
rationale: Facultative organisms grow with or without oxygen but grow better at the oxygen-rich top.
mediaNote: Thioglycolate tube-pattern figure, PDF slide corresponding to transcript 19:03-20:28.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: Uniform growth is aerotolerant anaerobe behavior; it does not use oxygen.

stem: An organism grows as a subsurface band in thioglycolate broth and fails to grow at the oxygen-rich surface. Which oxygen category fits best?
rationale: Microaerophiles require some oxygen, but excessive oxygen is toxic, producing a band partway down the tube.
mediaNote: Thioglycolate tube-pattern figure, PDF slide corresponding to transcript 19:03-20:28.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: Obligate aerobes grow at the top where oxygen is highest.

stem: A fungal preparation shows multicellular branching filaments that together form a mycelium. Which form is present?
rationale: Molds are multicellular and consist of hyphae that form a mycelium.
mediaNote: Review fungal morphology figure in source section V.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: Yeasts are unicellular and reproduce by budding.

stem: A chain of elongated fungal cells has recurrent pinched constrictions at each junction. What is it?
rationale: Pseudohyphae have recurrent bud-like/pinched constrictions, unlike true hyphae.
mediaNote: True-hypha versus pseudohypha figure in source section V.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: True hyphae lack the repeated constrictions.

stem: A fungal micrograph shows asexual spores enclosed within a sac-like structure at the end of a hypha. Which structure is being identified?
rationale: Sporangiospores are enclosed within a sac-like sporangium. Conidia are borne externally from a hypha or conidiophore.
sourceRef: Fungal Pathogens PDF p. 11; docx V.F
mediaNote: Use the source reproductive-structure figure on PDF p. 11; the image must be shown without answer-revealing labels.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: A conidiophore bears conidia externally rather than enclosing them within a sac.

stem: A beta-lactam stops bacterial cell-wall crosslink formation. Which enzyme was inhibited?
rationale: Beta-lactams bind PBPs/transpeptidases to prevent peptidoglycan crosslinking.
mediaNote: Peptidoglycan synthesis diagram on PDF slide 11.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: Lysozyme is host enzyme that cleaves glycan chains, not the beta-lactam target.

stem: Which blood-film approach should be chosen when maximal detection sensitivity is the priority?
rationale: Thick smears maximize sensitivity; thin smears preserve morphology and permit quantification.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: Thin smears favor ultrastructure and quantification.

stem: Which feature is the principal advantage of a thin blood smear?
rationale: The outline assigns ultrastructure and quantification to thin smears.

closestDistractor.why_wrong: Maximum sensitivity is the thick-smear advantage.

stem: Which trigger initiates the classical complement pathway?
options: C3b bound spontaneously to a microbial surface
rationale: Classical complement is initiated when C1 binds antibody on bacterial surface; alternative uses C3b and lectin uses MBL.
